name: Crown lengthening / gingivectomy
lead: Crown lengthening exposes more tooth by removing gum tissue and sometimes supporting bone, and is done for functional or aesthetic reasons, including gummy smile.[1] Gingivectomy is the removal of part of the gum tissue and is described as the oldest surgical approach in periodontal therapy.[2]

Both are established dental procedures used for restorative and periodontal reasons; their use for smile aesthetics is the part relevant to looksmaxxing. Registered trials in 2011-2026 compare techniques such as flapless, piezoelectric, laser and digitally guided approaches.[3][4][5]
infobox: Gingivectomy, flap with bone recontouring, forced eruption, laser

paras: Crown lengthening may be done surgically by an apically repositioned flap with bone recontouring, or orthodontically by forced tooth eruption.[1] Gingivectomy can be performed with a scalpel, electrosurgery or laser.[2]

Wikipedia states that up to about 3 mm of gum display when smiling is considered acceptable and more is often regarded as unaesthetic, and that gingivectomy can address it.[2] Aesthetic planning must consider smile line, lip position and tooth proportions.[2] Trials treat conditions such as altered passive eruption.[6][7]

Described drawbacks include encroaching on the supracrestal tissue attachment, weakening adjacent teeth by removing bone, bone loss that is hard to restore, and postoperative pain with the flap technique.[1] For gingivectomy, recurrence, black triangles and return of disease with poor hygiene are described.[2]

Registered trials include a comparison of periodontal plastic surgery techniques for gummy smile (n=30),[8] digitally guided versus conventional crown lengthening,[9][10] flapless esthetic crown lengthening for excessive gingival display (n=28, 2011),[11] closed piezoelectric versus open flap approaches,[12][13] Er:YAG laser versus surgical crown lengthening,[4] and periodontal stability after correcting altered passive eruption.[7] Published results are not summarised in the sources used.

card.summary: Dental surgery that trims gum (and sometimes bone) to expose more tooth, used for gummy smiles when the gum line is the cause.
card.note: Bone removal is irreversible and can affect adjacent teeth.

quick.overview:
Crown lengthening and gingivectomy remove gum tissue, and in some cases bone, to expose more of the teeth. They are standard periodontal procedures also used to reduce gum display in a smile.

Registered trials compare surgical, flapless, piezoelectric, laser and digitally guided methods.
quick.mechanism: Gum is trimmed or repositioned, with bone recontouring if needed, so the gum line sits higher on the teeth.
quick.risks: Described drawbacks include irreversible bone loss, weakening of neighbouring teeth, pain with flap surgery, recurrence and black triangles.
